questions.prompt: Which problem does sharding solve that adding read replicas does not?

options.text: Too many reads of the same popular rows
More writes, or more data, than one leader machine can handle
Slow network between users and the data center

questions.explanation: Replicas copy all the data and all the writes, so they add read capacity only. Sharding splits data and writes across machines.

questions.prompt: A metrics database is range-partitioned by timestamp. What goes wrong?

options.text: All new writes land on the shard that owns the current time, creating a hot spot

questions.explanation: New data always has the latest timestamp, so one shard takes every write. Prefixing the key with a sensor id, for example, spreads writes while keeping each sensor's data in time order.

questions.prompt: Keys are placed with hash(key) mod N. You grow from 4 to 5 shards. Roughly what share of keys must move?
questions.explanation: A key stays only if hash mod 4 equals hash mod 5, which is true for 4 of every 20 hash values: 20%. The other 80% move. Consistent hashing would move only about 20%.

questions.prompt: Why give each machine many virtual nodes on a consistent hashing ring? Select all that apply.

options.text: Load evens out because each machine owns many small arcs
A leaving machine's keys spread over many machines instead of one neighbour
Bigger machines can take a bigger share by having more virtual nodes

questions.explanation: Many points per machine smooth out random arc sizes, scatter a departing machine's load, and allow weighting. Lookups still hash the key.

questions.prompt: A chat app stores billions of messages. Most reads load the latest messages of one conversation. Which shard key fits best?

options.text: Conversation id, hashed, with messages ordered by time within the shard
The date the message was sent

questions.explanation: Hashing the conversation id spreads conversations evenly and keeps each one on a single shard, so the common read is a single-shard query. Message id scatters a conversation, country has few, uneven values, and date makes today's shard hot.
